section_summary: This section contains three 1937 consular despatches concerning Chinese labor migration through Dairen into Manchuria. The first two provide quarterly statistics, discuss labor shortages and immigration quotas, and include tables organized by embarkation port; the third announces suspension of the reports after local authorities classified the figures as military secrets. A final 1933 departmental note comments on a despatch about the Grand Manchurian Exposition.

subfiles.title: Chinese Coolie Immigration and Emigration Through Dairen, First Quarter of 1937
subfiles.from: Stuart E. Grummon, American Consul at Dairen
subfiles.to: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador at Tokyo
subfiles.about: Reports Chinese labor arrivals and departures through Dairen during the first quarter of 1937.
subfiles.summary: First quarter 1937: 65,902 Chinese laborers arrived through Dairen; Five-Year Plan labor shortages and proposals to raise quotas; table of arrivals, departures and net increase for 1931-1936.

subfiles.title: Chinese Coolie Immigration and Emigration Through Dairen, Second Quarter of 1937
subfiles.from: Stuart E. Grummon, American Consul at Dairen
subfiles.to: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador at Tokyo
subfiles.about: Reports Chinese labor migration through Dairen during April–June 1937 and analyzes labor demand in Manchuria.
subfiles.summary: Second quarter 1937: immigration peaked in May and fell in June; 61,622 arrivals and 29,589 departures; Dairen handled about 40 percent of entering laborers; shortages and rumors of higher quotas.

subfiles.title: Temporary Discontinuance of Quarterly Reports on Chinese Coolie Immigration and Emigration Through Dairen
subfiles.from: Stuart E. Grummon, American Consul at Dairen
subfiles.to: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador at Tokyo
subfiles.about: Announces the suspension of quarterly migration reports after Dairen authorities classified the underlying statistics as military secrets.
subfiles.summary: Dairen police refused third-quarter migration figures as militarily sensitive; Grummon suggests many laborers returned to China, causing stevedore shortages and ships waiting outside the harbor.

subfiles.title: Departmental Note on the Grand Manchurian Exposition
subfiles.from: Department of State, Division of Far Eastern Affairs
subfiles.about: Comments on an August 22, 1933, Dairen despatch describing the Grand Manchurian Exposition.
subfiles.summary: Note: the Grand Manchurian Exposition is unimportant but the despatch shows an interesting educational method.
